newsitem.title: GAMBIA: Gambia army ruler takes slim early poll lead.
newsitem.headline: Gambia army ruler takes slim early poll lead.

text.p: Gambia's military ruler took a slim lead over his toughest civilian challenger in the first constituency declared in presidential elections.
Yahya Jammeh polled 556 votes or 54 percent of ballots cast in Janjanbureh, the West African country's smallest constituency.
His chief rival, lawyer Ousainou Darboe polled 423 votes or 41 percent, according to results from the electoral commission PIEC broadcast on state television on Thursday.

Of the two other civilian candidates, generally seen as marginal in the election, hotel manager Amath Bah of the National Reconciliation Party (NRP) scored 27 votes while Sidia Jatta of the small People's Democratic Organisation for Independence and Socialism was fourth with 15 votes.
Janjanbureh was also the first constituency to be declared in last month's national referendum when Jammeh won a 38 percent "Yes" vote countrywide for a new constitution.

Final results were expected late on Friday with a close race forecast between Jammeh and Darboe, who is leader of the United Democratic Party. Jammeh is a candidate of the Alliance for Patriotic Reorientation and Construction.
